title: Functions & Parameters: Reusable Logic & Returns
description: Master JavaScript functions: parameter passing, explicit return statements vs console.log side effects, call expression value substitution, and modular program design.

objectives.statement: Author reusable JavaScript functions that accept parameters and calculate values.
Use explicit return statements to pass computed values back to caller expressions.

content.title: Packaging Reusable Logic
content.hook: Instead of copy-pasting the same 10 lines of code across your project, functions allow you to write logic once and reuse it anywhere with different inputs.
content.context: A function takes inputs (parameters), performs computation, and returns an output via the return keyword. The return value replaces the function call expression where it was invoked.
goals: Distinguish return values (data output) from console.log (terminal printing).
Understand how call expressions substitute with their returned values.

content.title: The Function Black Box
content.description: Inputs (Arguments) pass into Parameters -> Internal execution frame computes value -> Explicit 'return' delivers output back to the calling expression in place of the call.

content.prompt: What greeting string will be printed to the console?
content.explanation: formatGreeting('Sarah', 'Captain') assigns name = 'Sarah' and role = 'Captain', returning 'Captain Sarah'.

feedback.correct: Spot on! The parameters are concatenated into 'Captain Sarah' and returned to greeting.
feedback.incorrect: Check parameter order: role is the second argument ('Captain'), concatenated before name ('Sarah').

content.question: What does a JavaScript function return if it finishes execution without hitting an explicit `return` statement?
content.explanation: Any function without an explicit return statement automatically evaluates to undefined when called.

feedback.correct: Correct! JavaScript functions default to returning undefined when no return statement is executed.
feedback.incorrect: Remember that missing return statements yield undefined, not null or 0.

content.title: Functions Mastered
takeaways: Functions encapsulate reusable computational logic with named parameters.
return delivers data back to the calling expression; console.log only prints to DevTools.
Functions without explicit returns implicitly evaluate to undefined.
